On Thursday, November 12 (08:47–12:27 UTC), `ingest` v2.14.0 (PR `ingest#412`) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB and rolled out to all pods at once [1]. With a 512 Mi memory limit, the `ingest-worker` pods ran out of memory on the first large batch and crash-looped, causing consumer lag and stale customer dashboards for 3h40 [1][5].

No customer data was lost [1][3]. Events continued arriving in Kafka and were processed late after a rollback to v2.13.3 [1]; a November 13 reconciliation confirmed that event counts per workspace matched Kafka offsets [1][3].

The following changes are being made:
- **Reverted batch size and added a memory guard (`ingest#419`, merged Nov 13):** Restored the default `max_batch_bytes` to 1 MB, updated the batcher to reject batches larger than 25% of the container memory limit with a warning, and kept 10 MB only via explicit config for bulk imports running on the 2 Gi pool [1][23].
- **Consumer lag alerting (`KES-431`, due Nov 20):** Added an on-call alert for `ingest-events` consumer lag exceeding 5 minutes, which is currently being tuned so it does not trigger during nightly backfills [1][6].
- **Canary config rollouts (`KES-432`, due Nov 27):** Send ingest configuration changes to the canary pool first [1].
- **Higher memory limit and load testing (`KES-433`, due Nov 27):** Raise the worker memory limit to 1 Gi and add a load test covering batch sizes [1].
